schemeDeck.name: Composite scheme of arrangement investor presentation (board approval 9-Jan-2026)

profile: India's largest mid-market hotel chain: owns, leases, manages and franchises hotels under Aurika (upscale), Lemon Tree Premier (upper midscale), Lemon Tree Hotels (midscale), Red Fox (economy) and Keys (Prima, Select, Lite). 135 operating hotels / 11,946 rooms in 80+ cities at 30-Jun-2026 (India, Dubai, Bhutan, Nepal); 41 owned or leased hotels / 5,759 rooms, 94 managed or franchised / 6,187 rooms; signed pipeline 144 hotels / 11,435 rooms. Owned hotels sit mostly in Fleur Hotels (58.91% Lemon Tree, 41.09% Warburg Pincus since 22-May-2026; APG before), plus Carnation (management company), Keys hotels and 100% subsidiaries.

underDevelopment: Aurika, Nehru Place, Delhi (leased from DDA)
final approvals pending; capex to be announced

kpis.note: Company 'total revenue' and 'net EBITDA' include other income (FY26 Rs8.2 cr); ARR and occupancy are for owned and leased hotels. FY25 fees backed out from FY26 growth (+23% / +8%).

scheme.steps: Step 1: Carnation Hotels and Hamstede Living merge into Lemon Tree. Part A: four 100% subsidiaries (Oriole Dr. Fresh, Sukhsagar Complexes, Manakin Resorts, Canary Hotels; 4 hotels, 359 rooms) merge into Fleur for 0.58 cr Fleur shares to Lemon Tree. Part B: 11 operating hotels (1,204 rooms), Aurika Shimla, the Shillong investment and the development team are demerged into Fleur; Lemon Tree shareholders get 20 Fleur shares for every 311 Lemon Tree shares (5.09 cr Fleur shares). Fleur then lists.
scheme.wpPrimary: Up to Rs960 cr of equity into Fleur, in tranches, before listing; it will raise Warburg's stake and dilute Lemon Tree's (Q1 call: 'USD100 million ... Lemon Tree is 41% on 110, Warburg 36% on 110').
scheme.status: At 30-Sep-2026: CCI approved (7-Apr-2026); Warburg bought APG's 41.09% (22-May-2026); with SEBI and the exchanges for scrutiny; NCLT filing, shareholder and creditor meetings still to come. Management: completion and Fleur listing 'conservatively ... in the late second half of next year' (CY2027; CFO hoped for H1). CRISIL (17-Jul-2026): 9-12 months.
scheme.src: schemeDeck slides 6-9, 27-28; q4call; q1deck slide 75; q1call; ar26; crisil

guidance.margin: Net EBITDA margin: FY27 'will be well better than' 47%; FY28 'if we do not do 50%, then we have underperformed' (Executive Chairman, 10-Aug-2026). Renovation + technology + GST costs 5.8% of revenue in FY26, guided to ~3.7% from FY28 (q1deck slide 21; q4call).
guidance.demand: Q1 hit by the West Asia conflict (weaker corporate travel, Mumbai and Gurugram soft); 'July was great ... August continues to be solid'; Q2 onwards double-digit growth expected (q1call).
guidance.fees: ~2,000 managed / franchised keys to open in FY27 (334 in Q1); ~5,000 signed in FY26 should open around FY29; long-term management business EBITDA margin 75-80%.
guidance.keys: Keys portfolio target ~Rs115-120 cr revenue and ~Rs60 cr EBITDA once renovated (2/3 done at Jun-26).
guidance.capex: CRISIL: Rs90-100 cr a year in FY27-29 (about 250 premium keys); renovation opex + capex to fall towards ~1% of revenue from FY28 (q1call).
guidance.debt: Gross debt Rs1,475 cr at Jun-26 (Rs1,275 cr net of ~Rs200 cr cash); aim to be debt-free at Lemon Tree in 3-4 years (CRISIL); post-scheme all debt sits in Fleur, target ~2x debt/EBITDA.

history: Company founded in 2002 by Patanjali Keswani (earlier with the Taj group and A.T. Kearney); first hotel (49 rooms) opens in 2004
Warburg Pincus invests in Lemon Tree (it later exited fully)
Red Fox (2009) and Lemon Tree Premier (2010) launched; APG invests in Fleur Hotels, the asset-owning platform (2012)
Acquires Keys Hotels; Aurika brand launched; first overseas hotel (Dubai)
Covid: revenue Rs252 cr in FY21 (−62%); attributable losses of Rs127 cr and Rs87 cr
Aurika, Mumbai Skycity (owned via Fleur) becomes operational; finance and depreciation costs rise
Large renovation programme (Keys, Red Fox, older Lemon Trees) expensed through opex; GST change in Sep-2025 removes input credit on rooms below Rs7,500 (half-year effect in FY26)
Board approves the composite scheme: Lemon Tree to become asset-light, Fleur the listed owner; Warburg Pincus to buy APG's 41.09% of Fleur and commit up to Rs960 cr
Warburg Pincus completes the purchase of APG's Fleur stake; APG keeps 14.99% of Lemon Tree

accounting.renovation: Renovation is mostly expensed (opex), not capitalised: renovation + technology + GST impact was 5.8% of revenue in FY26 (renovation ~4.2%, technology ~0.6%, GST ~1.0% for half a year; Q1FY27 deck slide 21), which depresses reported margins while the programme runs.
accounting.ebitdaDefinition: The company's 'net EBITDA' includes other income (FY26 Rs8.2 cr); Screener operating EBITDA excludes it (Rs690 cr).
accounting.exceptional: FY26 exceptional charge Rs33.3 cr (new labour codes, Q3FY26) and Rs1.9 cr in Q4; Screener after-tax Rs23 cr.
accounting.sar: Stock appreciation rights (cash-settled): provision Rs2.6 cr in Q1FY27, marked to the share price.

icraSep26.note: premium hotels; as used in the EIHOTEL and INDHOTEL reports

industry.midMarket: Lemon Tree argues India's mid-market is supply-short: branded supply is a fraction of demand in tier-2/3 cities, and its 45% repeat demand and 2.5 m loyalty members let it fill new managed hotels fast (q1call; ar26 industry section).
industry.gst: From late Sep-2025 rooms below Rs7,500 a night lost GST input credit (half-year effect in FY26); Lemon Tree lost ~2.3% of revenue in Q1FY27 (q1deck slide 16), guided to ~2% in FY27 and ~1.7% in FY28 (ICICI Direct, 11-Aug-2026).
